saints.name: St. Josaphat
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The Ruthenian archbishop and monk who gave his life for the union of the Eastern Church with Rome…
biography: Born about 1580 at Volodymyr in Volhynia and baptized John Kuncevyc, he became a monk of the Byzantine rite and took the name Josaphat, embracing the Union of Brest by which many Ruthenians were reconciled with the See of Rome while keeping their Eastern liturgy. He was made Archbishop of Polotsk.

His zeal for the union drew fierce opposition, and on 12 November 1623 he was killed by a mob at Vitebsk, dying a martyr for Christian unity. He was the first saint of the Eastern Church to be formally canonized by Rome. He is honoured as a patron of Christian unity between East and West.
saints.knownFor: Martyrdom for the union of the Eastern churches with Rome.
